title: Session launching and tracking
summary: Wave 1 design foundation complete. Wave 2 pivots to a local-first manual session registry (issue #9) to deliver restart-resilient session tracking ahead of the launch pipeline. Launch-from-graph and graph overlay follow in Waves 3-4.

nodes.title: Bootstrap design docs
nodes.summary: Create Streamliner's repo-scoped docs/design set from the current root docs and switch this workstream to reference that design layer.

nodes.title: Make workstream design explicit
nodes.summary: Run explicit design sessions for the full workstream so the launch contract, key design decisions, and downstream issue-graph adjustments are written down before more implementation issues are finalized.

nodes.title: Registry-first reorientation
nodes.summary: Reorient the workstream so a manual session registry ships before the launch pipeline. Captures the shift to treating the registry as the primary session surface (graph overlay becomes a projection of it) and reshapes the downstream nodes accordingly. Landed Decision 004 (docs/design/decisions/004-session-registry-primary-surface.md) alongside the brief/graph updates.

nodes.title: Session registry model
nodes.summary: Define the local-first session registry: persisted record shape (id, title, description, color, cwd, repo, status, last-seen, tags), storage layout under the runtime-state root (per-session JSON + index), autosave semantics, and the observation hook that imports existing Copilot CLI sessions from their session state files per decision #001.

nodes.title: Manual session registry UI
nodes.summary: Ship a flat 'my sessions' UI surface decoupled from the graph: list every tracked session, edit title/description, assign colors, mark paused/ended/archived, autosave on change. Imports are populated from the observation hook; manual entries are also supported for sessions not yet discoverable.

nodes.title: Session relaunch
nodes.summary: Reopen a tracked session after a restart: open a terminal at the recorded cwd and, when the Copilot CLI session id is still resolvable, resume that session directly. Minimum viable version just restores the tab at the right cwd with the assigned color; Copilot CLI resume is a stretch within the same node. Backend action is independent of the registry UI and can land in parallel.

nodes.title: Windows Terminal color bridge spike
nodes.summary: Spike feasibility of reflecting the registry's assigned color into Windows Terminal (tab title + tabColor via profile or wt.exe args). Decide whether Wave 2 ships the bridge or defers it. Independent of the registry UI and relaunch work.

nodes.title: Backend context assembly
nodes.summary: Assemble the Layer 0-3 launch payload inputs on the backend per the session system design: read design docs, extract brief sections, and resolve node specs so the SDK launch-prep step can write the context files after paw-init creates the PAW work directory.

nodes.title: Launch claim binding
nodes.summary: Record launch claims before terminal startup and bind discovered sessions using a launch nonce plus cwd/branch/window guardrails so the visible Copilot CLI session attaches to the correct graph node. Launched sessions also register into the Wave 2 session registry rather than introducing a parallel tracking surface. Independent of the SDK-prep chain and can land in parallel.

nodes.title: Copilot SDK launch prep plumbing
nodes.summary: Use Copilot SDK on the backend to gather context, run paw-init in the target repo, write context files, and return the launch spec before the Copilot CLI worker session starts.

nodes.title: Terminal launch integration
nodes.summary: Launch a visible Copilot CLI interactive session from the graph with the prepared kickoff prompt so the operator can watch and intervene in the PAW session as needed. Creates/updates the corresponding registry entry on launch and consumes the bound launch claim.

nodes.title: Session event observation
nodes.summary: Observe Copilot session runtime: turn boundaries from events.jsonl, hook signal files, and derived idle/needs-input state. Extends the registry's import hook with full lifecycle tracking.

nodes.title: PAW control-state observation
nodes.summary: Read PAW `## Control State` (including `Workflow Identity`) from `WorkflowContext.md` / `ReviewContext.md` as the workflow progression source per decision #003, with legacy artifact inference as fallback. Runs in parallel with event-based session observation; the two are orthogonal inputs into the overlay.

nodes.title: Runtime overlay in UI
nodes.summary: Project registry entries, event observation state, and PAW control state onto the committed graph in the UI, combining committed node status with runtime session status per the overlay model in the session system design. The overlay is a view over the registry, not a parallel store.

nodes.title: Launch and tracking usable on the graph
nodes.summary: A node can launch a PAW session into a visible terminal and Streamliner can show live runtime state for that node on the graph by projecting the session registry plus observed state, without committing telemetry into the workstream artifacts.

checkpoints.title: Design foundation aligned
checkpoints.summary: Repo-scoped design docs exist and the workstream's explicit design direction is captured.

checkpoints.title: Manual session registry usable
checkpoints.summary: Streamliner persists a local, graph-independent registry of Copilot sessions with autosaved titles/descriptions/colors and can relaunch them after a restart.

checkpoints.title: Launch from graph works
checkpoints.summary: Streamliner assembles context, runs paw-init, binds a launch claim in parallel, compiles the kickoff prompt, and launches a visible Copilot CLI interactive session from a node, registering it into the Wave 2 registry.

checkpoints.title: Tracking visible on the graph
checkpoints.summary: Streamliner overlays the registry, event observation, and PAW control state onto the graph without turning graph.json into a telemetry log.
